Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Compare the differential genes on global proteome level and glycoproteome level for IPMN vs ND.  Provide a pathway level summary of biological functions of upregulated or downregulated glycopeptides whose global protein expression remained unchanged.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
In Wang et al. (2025), global proteomics (Table S2A) and site-specific glycoproteomics (Table S3I) were performed on surgically resected intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) versus matched normal duct (ND) tissues. A total of 9 417 proteins (global) and 85 glycopeptides (glycoproteome) were quantified. Differential analysis (IPMN vs ND) identified many significantly up- and down-regulated proteins and glycopeptides. Here, we focus on glycopeptides significantly up- or down-regulated (FDR < 0.05) whose parent proteins showed no significant change at the global level (FDR ≥ 0.05).

Keywords  
• Glycosylation • IPMN • Glycoproteomics • Amino-acid metabolism • Sterol homeostasis  

Candidate Genes  
CPD, DDAH1, ERLIN2, GUSB, TSPAN13  

Pathway-Level Summary (Proteins with significant glycosite change but global expression unchanged)  
We took the list of glycoproteins with significant site-specific up-/down-regulation (n = 57 distinct proteins), filtered for those whose global protein FDR ≥ 0.05 (n = 42), and performed ORA (GO_BP, Reactome, Hallmark). Top enriched processes cluster into four functional modules:

1. Amino-acid metabolism & vascular tone  
   – Terms: Regulation of cellular response to hypoxia; Citrulline metabolic process; Arginine catabolic/metabolic processes; Glutamine family amino‐acid catabolism; Negative regulation of vascular permeability; eNOS Activation  
   – Leading gene: DDAH1  

2. Sterol/lipid homeostasis  
   – Terms: SREBP signaling; Regulation of sterol biosynthetic process; Cellular response to sterol depletion; Regulation of cholesterol/FA biosynthesis  
   – Leading gene: ERLIN2  

3. Glycan catabolism & extracellular matrix turnover  
   – Terms: Glycoside/glycosaminoglycan/aminoglycan catabolic processes; Hyaluronan uptake and degradation; Mucopolysaccharidoses  
   – Leading gene: GUSB  

4. Alcohol biosynthesis regulation & monooxygenase activity  
   – Terms: Regulation of alcohol biosynthetic process; Negative regulation of alcohol biosynthesis; Regulation of monooxygenase activity  
   – Leading gene: ERLIN2  

Complete Top ORA Terms (FDR < 0.05):  
| Term                                                       | Leading gene(s) | Category                          | ORA Adjusted P-value |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------|
| Regulation Of Cellular Response To Hypoxia (GO:1900037)    | DDAH1           | Amino-acid/Vascular module        | 0.0123               |
| Citrulline Metabolic Process (GO:0000052)                  | DDAH1           | Amino-acid module                 | 0.0123               |
| Arginine Catabolic Process (GO:0006527)                    | DDAH1           | Amino-acid module                 | 0.0123               |
| Glutamine Family Amino Acid Catabolic Process (GO:0009065) | DDAH1           | Amino-acid module                 | 0.0123               |
| eNOS Activation (Reactome)                                 | DDAH1           | Amino-acid/Vascular module        | 0.0331               |
| Negative Regulation Of Vascular Permeability (GO:0043116)  | DDAH1           | Amino-acid/Vascular module        | 0.0123               |
| SREBP Signaling Pathway (GO:0032933)                       | ERLIN2          | Sterol/Lipid module               | 0.0123               |
| Regulation Of Sterol Biosynthetic Process (GO:0106118)     | ERLIN2          | Sterol/Lipid module               | 0.0123               |
| Cellular Response To Sterol Depletion (GO:0071501)         | ERLIN2          | Sterol/Lipid module               | 0.0123               |
| Regulation Of Cholesterol Biosynthetic Process (GO:0045540)| ERLIN2          | Sterol/Lipid module               | 0.0123               |
| Negative Regulation Of Fatty Acid Biosynthetic Process     | ERLIN2          | Sterol/Lipid module               | 0.0123               |
| Glycoside Catabolic Process (GO:0016139)                   | GUSB            | Glycan Catabolism module          | 0.0123               |
| Aminoglycan Catabolic Process (GO:0006026)                 | GUSB            | Glycan Catabolism module          | 0.0123               |
| Glycosaminoglycan Catabolic Process (GO:0006027)           | GUSB            | Glycan Catabolism module          | 0.0123               |
| Hyaluronan Uptake and Degradation (Reactome)               | GUSB            | Glycan Catabolism module          | 0.0331               |
| Mucopolysaccharidoses (Reactome)                           | GUSB            | Glycan Catabolism module          | 0.0331               |
| Regulation Of Alcohol Biosynthetic Process                 | ERLIN2          | Monooxygenase/Alcohol module      | 0.0123               |
| Negative Regulation Of Alcohol Biosynthetic Process        | ERLIN2          | Monooxygenase/Alcohol module      | 0.0123               |
| Regulation Of Monooxygenase Activity                       | DDAH1           | Monooxygenase/Alcohol module      | 0.0123               |

Interpretation  
The unchanged global abundances of CPD, DDAH1, ERLIN2, GUSB, TSPAN13, etc., mask pronounced remodeling at their glycosylation sites. DDAH1 glyco-upregulation implicates local control of nitric oxide bioavailability and arginine turnover in IPMN microenvironments, potentially modulating vascular permeability under hypoxia. ERLIN2 glycosite alterations enrich SREBP-driven sterol homeostasis and xenobiotic/monooxygenase regulation, hinting at membrane lipid remodeling. GUSB glyco-upregulation highlights enhanced extracellular matrix turnover and glycosaminoglycan degradation—a hallmark of tissue remodeling in premalignant lesions. TSPAN13 and CPD, though glyco-regulated, did not yield strong pathway hits by ORA, suggesting less well-annotated functions. Overall, site-specific glycoproteome changes reveal metabolic, lipid, and microenvironmental adaptations not apparent at the total‐protein level.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate DDAH1 and ERLIN2 glycosylation changes by targeted Glyco-MS and assess impact on enzyme activity.  
2. Quantify nitric oxide and glycosaminoglycan turnover in IPMN cyst fluid to link DDAH1 and GUSB changes to fluid biochemistry.  
3. Investigate CPD and TSPAN13 glyco-functions via glyco-mutagenesis to uncover novel IPMN biomarkers.  
4. Assess broader sterol‐regulatory network via transcriptomics to confirm ERLIN2 glyco-driven SREBP signaling.
